content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"C2BMC is the integrating element of the Missile Defense System — a combat-proven operational system that enables the U.S. President, Secretary of Defense, and Combatant Commanders to see the battle develop, dynamically manage networked sensors, and coordinate weapons systems against a diverse range of missile threats.","citation":{"fact_id":"7175acc175e205c2"}},{"text":"Systems linked to C2BMC include Patriot, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD), Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense, Aegis Ashore, Ground-based Midcourse Defense (GMD), the Army Integrated Air and Missile Defense Battle Command System, and sensors such as the AN/TPY-2 radar, Sea-Based X-Band Radar, Long Range Discrimination Radar, and Space-Based Infrared System.","citation":{"fact_id":"7175acc175e205c2"}},{"text":"The program is run by the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) and is funded through the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Defense-Wide account.","citation":{"fact_id":"44df4dbd7791ddd1"}},{"text":"C2BMC delivers capabilities incrementally with each software build (called a Spiral or Capability Build), each one adding to or enhancing the capability of the previous build — for example, Spiral 8.2 provides Homeland Defense for increased GMD battlespace and improved threat tracking using multiple sensors communicating via Link-16.","citation":{"fact_id":"7175acc175e205c2"}},{"text":"The program is organized into projects including Command & Control, Battle Management, Communications (project MD01), C2BMC Development Support (MX01), C2BMC Test (MT01), Cyber Operations (MC01), and Program-Wide Support (MD40).","citation":{"fact_id":"4b0acd87fc398bc5"}},{"text":"Under the MDA's Defense of Guam Program, C2BMC is integrating Missile Defense and Joint systems, establishing a permanent Command Center, and providing communication support throughout the island.","citation":{"fact_id":"7175acc175e205c2"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"For fiscal year 2026, the total budget request for C2BMC is about $1.067 billion (in USD thousands, $1,067,183).","citation":{"fact_id":"d24314146cbc5dd5"}},{"text":"That total is nearly double the roughly $551.8 million enacted for fiscal year 2025 — a jump of about $515.4 million.","citation":{"fact_id":"a49212c5260c7fea"}},{"text":"The FY2026 total is split between a $634.183 million discretionary request and a $433 million reconciliation request.","citation":{"fact_id":"86950f799c22eb3e"}},{"text":"The reconciliation portion of the FY2026 request totals $433 million (USD thousands).","citation":{"fact_id":"665674c4dd265658"}},{"text":"In FY2024, the program spent about $540.2 million (actuals).","citation":{"fact_id":"9fc6c4a8ba7aff47"}},{"text":"MDA states that rapidly evolving rogue and peer missile threats have led to a change in national defense policy, and that the President's January 27, 2025 Executive Order established a goal of protecting U.S. citizens, safeguarding critical infrastructure, and securing second-strike capability against missile attack — with the budget submission reflecting changes to meet this evolving mission.","citation":{"fact_id":"7175acc175e205c2"}},{"text":"The C2BMC Command Center provides continuous 24-hours-a-day, 7-days-a-week Ballistic Missile Defense Systems operations, including system and network monitoring and network defense against cyber-attacks.","citation":{"fact_id":"7175acc175e205c2"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"Lobbying filings from Lockheed Martin Corporation in 2024 referenced missile defense matters, described as \"F-35 funding, Army Missile Defense.\"","citation":{"fact_id":"0660b6f1a3db335b"}},{"text":"A 2024 Lockheed Martin filing referenced the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2025, matching on the terms \"Missile\" and \"Communications.\"","citation":{"fact_id":"00391cfca9eedb15"}},{"text":"A 2025 Lockheed Martin filing referenced the Streamlining Procurement for Effective Execution and Delivery and National Defense Authorization Act, matching on the terms \"Missile\" and \"Battle.\"","citation":{"fact_id":"04eea92ddae3e4b9"}},{"text":"A 2026 Lockheed Martin filing referenced the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026, including issues related to space and missile defense.","citation":{"fact_id":"002d7f7f516bc2f9"}},{"text":"Boeing Company filings in 2024 referenced the FY24 Department of Defense Appropriations Act, matching on the terms \"Missile\" and \"Communications.\"","citation":{"fact_id":"005fc74423472220"}},{"text":"A 2024 Boeing filing referenced FY24 supplemental appropriations and the FY25 Department of Defense Appropriations Act.","citation":{"fact_id":"0196f789fa9e481e"}}]},"recent_developments":{"claims":[]}}
